transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my right knee — the pain in it has been getting worse and it's really bothering me now. It's making it hard to get around.
Can you tell me when the knee pain first started and how it came on — and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It only started getting bad last week. And yes, penicillin gives me a rash.
Can you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started recently—including doses if you know them—and about any other health problems, operations, or hospital stays you've had?

I take metformin 1 gram twice a day, aspirin 75 milligrams once a day, atorvastatin 40 milligrams at night, and ramipril 5 milligrams once a day. I've had type 2 diabetes for about 10 years, and I had a stent put in a heart artery 6 years ago.
Besides the pain, have you noticed anything else going on with your right knee?
It sometimes swells up a bit by the evening, and it feels stiff in the mornings for about 20 minutes. But there's no redness, no fever, and it doesn't lock up.
What have you noticed that makes your knee pain better or worse?
It's worse going down the stairs and after I've been walking more than about 10 minutes. Rest and paracetamol help settle it.
What worries you most about your right knee?
I'd like something stronger for the pain, and I'm wondering whether I might end up needing a knee replacement. It's getting to the point where I can't even walk the dog round the park anymore.
Are there any other medicines you take that we haven't already talked about?
No, that's the lot — those are all the medicines I take.
How bad is your knee pain these days, and how much is it affecting your everyday life?
On bad days it's about a 7 out of 10, and I can't walk the dog round the park anymore. I've also started going down the stairs one step at a time holding the rail, which I never used to do.
Besides your diabetes and the heart stent, is there anything else in your past health — other illnesses, operations, or hospital stays — you'd like to add?
No, nothing else I can think of — just the diabetes and the heart stent.
Can you tell me what the pain in your right knee feels like, in your own words?
It's a deep, grinding sort of ache. It's on the inner side of the right knee, and it doesn't spread down my leg.
Is there anything else you'd like to add about your knee or any other changes you've noticed?
No, I don't think there's anything else.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
